Adding a new data source

Source: vignettes/adding-a-new-source.Rmd
adding-a-new-source.Rmd

rendehR ships MIMIC-III, MIMIC-IV, eICU and their demos. A new source is a registration plus four assets the pipeline reads: a source entry in the catalog, raw-loading rules, window SQL, and a concept overlay. The wizard scaffolds the files; this article explains what each one must contain.

What the wizard creates

add_source_wizard() writes a source directory with the files the pipeline looks for. Non-interactive use requires the hierarchy columns and the time origin, because those cannot be guessed:

add_source_wizard(
  name          = "my_ehr",
  root          = file.path(docs_root, "my-source"),
  select_id_cols = c("patient_id", "admission_id", "icu_id"),
  time_origin   = "admission_time",
  id_cols       = c(patient_id = "patient_id", admission_id = "admission_id",
                    icu_id = "icu_id"),
  cohort_key    = "admission_id",
  register      = FALSE
)

register = TRUE writes the catalog entry too. The generated window_tables.sql must define three relations; a source that omits one fails at the window stage:

  • admission_windows — one row per hospital admission;
  • icu_windows — one row per ICU stay;
  • visit_windows — the union used by cohort materialization and look-back.

The wizard’s output is a starting point: the column names in your raw tables and the catalog’s link keys still have to match your data.

The catalog entry

The catalog is inst/extdata/rendehr-data-source.json. An entry names the source family, its identifier columns, the tables that carry an ICU key, and the cohort_link_key that decides how clinical tables are filtered to the cohort. id_prefixes and demo_row_limit are optional.

The catalog is read from three places, first match wins: the project configuration, the directory in EHR_EXTERNAL_CONFIG_ROOT, and the package. A new source registered outside the package therefore needs EHR_EXTERNAL_CONFIG_ROOT set in the R session (for example in .Renviron); otherwise a fresh session falls back to the package catalog and does not know the source.

Raw data and concepts

download_source() knows the PhysioNet releases only. A new source’s raw files are yours to place; the pipeline reads them from raw_data_root using the catalog’s table and column rules. The wizard does not add a download route.

A concept overlay lives at <root>/rendehr_concepts_config.csv and covers the time-series dictionary. Duration concepts come from rendehr_duration_concepts_config.csv and are not scaffolded; add rows there for drug exposures the source can measure. Only the required fields are emitted as null; optional fields are omitted, so an overlay never silently blanks a package default. validate_concept_config() lists the overlay rows the concept stage would skip.

Subcohorts inside a source are materialized with materialize_subcohort(); they are not a per-source “variant” setting. The only per-source variant the wizard exposes is demo.row_limit, which caps a demo import.

Validate and run

validate_source_config() checks that the files the source declares exist. It does not prove the SQL returns matching columns, and download_source() does not accept a newly registered name. The first real test is an unfiltered DuckDB run, which is also the only pipeline path a newly registered family supports before its clinical SQL is written:

run_one_source("my_ehr", engine = "duckdb",
               stages = c("run_db", "build_cohort_info"))

Once the window tables and the concept overlay are in place, the usual cohort routes apply, and the source can take part in merge_sources() like any other.

The add-source assistant can produce the wizard call for you:

ehr_add_source_assistant(action = "script")

It returns the call as text; action = "write" asks it to create the files directly. State the action explicitly in scripts: the default is "write" in an interactive session and "script" otherwise.
